title: Handling the cards in the shop
target: How a card behaves as a physical object in TCG Card Shop Simulator, from picking it up to putting it on a shelf.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shelf or storage for them
The scanner if you are selling them

steps.do: Treat a card as a world object rather than a screen item.
steps.because: a card is a world object with a mesh, a highlight, a collider and a rigid body (InteractableCard3d, m_Mesh, m_HighlightGameObj, m_Collider, m_Rigidbody)

steps.do: Know which cards you can pick up, box and scan before you plan a job.
steps.because: a card carries its own permissions for being picked up and moved, boxed up and scanned at the counter (m_CanPickupMoveObject, m_CanBoxUpObject, m_CanScanByCounter)

steps.do: Watch where a card is allowed to be put.
steps.because: a card carries placement rules for the shop and for the warehouse, with a move area and a separate shelf move area (m_PlaceObjectInShopOnly, m_PlaceObjectInWarehouseOnly, m_MoveStateValidArea, m_ShelfMoveStateValidArea)

steps.do: Check whether a card belongs in an album before you shelve it as stock.
steps.because: a card carries a flag for whether it is an album card (m_IsCardAlbumCard)

steps.do: Know what the display group is doing while a card is shown.
steps.because: the group holds a card display and an animation of its own, with a front mesh position and a back mesh (Card3dUIGroup, m_CardUI, m_Anim, m_CardFrontMeshPos, m_CardBackMesh)

steps.do: Use the new-card mark to spot what you have just acquired.
steps.because: the group can mark a card as new (m_NewCardIndicator)

steps.do: Keep graded cards in the group that was built for them.
steps.because: there is a graded group and a separate cull group with a slab top-layer mesh and blockers for the case's front and back (m_GradedCardGrp, m_GradedCardCullGrp, m_SlabTopLayerMesh, m_GradedCaseCullCardFrontMeshBlocker, m_GradedCaseCullCardBackMeshBlocker)

commonMistakes: Trying to move a card that is not allowed to be picked up.
Putting a card where the card itself does not permit.
Shelving an album card as ordinary stock.
Treating a graded card like a loose one when it has its own display group.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
